description: Hello, we are a mostly female team that will be participating in the Nasa Space Apps for the City of Norwalk, CA. We are planning on doing the Information Jukebox and are interested in having more females join our team. We are part of SWE on campus and are looking to involve more females and grow our community of women in the engineering field.
summary: For our project we developed an interactive GUI system in which we had terrain sonification with the implementation of an Arduino. As you move the mouse over the terrain, the elevation follows a certain pitch and also corresponds to five different LED's which represent elevation ranges. This addresses the challenge as Earth information, in this case elevation of terrain, is demonstrated through audio pitches, and LCD and LED displays. This is important as it provides an interactive way for visually impaired, deaf, or able-bodied people to have a fun way to interact with information regarding the Earth's surface
details: Our project translates NASA's Earth terrain data to audio through a process called sonification, using Arduino Uno R3 and mouse control. When our mouse hovers over a specific terrain/coordinate on our global map software, the signal is omitted in three different ways: 1) through an LCD screen, where the audio is synchronized to the animated soundwaves it produces, 2) through the LED's, where they are placed accordingly to match the scaled legend we have on our software (green representing lowest terrain, and white representing highest,) 3) through the piezo passive buzzer, where it omits different tuned pitches depending on how high or low the terrain of the Earth is. For the software and hardware, python, C++, and Arduino IDE were all used. Our project is creative because we tailored it for different learners and those who are visually impaired but still interested in research. We believe that research should be accessible to everyone.
